resources.string: Normal nail plate formation
How the nail plate grows

A simplified lengthwise section of a human fingertip showing normal nail plate formation. Shapes and movement are not to scale, and chapter timing does not represent growth time. For anatomy education.
A lengthwise view

The proximal nail fold covers the root of the nail plate. The matrix lies at the root, the bed lies under the plate farther toward the fingertip, and the free edge extends past the bed. The moving highlight traces the plate.
New cells in the matrix
Living cells divide in the nail matrix beneath the root. Some of their descendants move toward the underside of the forming plate.
Cells become plate material
As these cells mature, they flatten, fill with hard keratins and lose their nuclei. They become part of the layered nail plate.
The plate moves toward the tip
New material joins the plate at the matrix, displacing the already-formed plate toward the fingertip. The small marks move with the plate to show that it advances together.
From nail bed to free edge
The nail bed supports the plate as it moves; the matrix remains its main source. Once the plate passes the end of the bed, it extends as the free edge. The tip does not make new plate.
